u1-l1.ahoj.note.en: For friends, family and children. It works for hello and goodbye, and so does **Čau!**
u1-l1.ahoj.note.t: Doʻstlar, oila aʼzolari va bolalar bilan. Salomlashganda ham, xayrlashganda ham aytiladi. **Čau!** ham xuddi shunday.

u1-l1.dobry-den.note.en: Literally “good day”: the polite hello for shops, strangers and teachers. With a name: **Dobrý deň, pán Kováč** (Mr Kováč).
u1-l1.dobry-den.note.t: Soʻzma-soʻz «xayrli kun». Doʻkonda, notanish odamlar va oʻqituvchilar bilan shunday salomlashiladi. Ism bilan: **Dobrý deň, pán Kováč** (janob Kovach).

u1-l1.choice-dobry-den.question.en: Emma walks into a bakery. What does she say?
u1-l1.choice-dobry-den.question.t: Emma novvoyxonaga kirdi. U nima deydi?

u1-l1.choice-dobry-den.why.en: In a shop, greet politely with **Dobrý deň**. Ahoj! is only for friends, family and children.
u1-l1.choice-dobry-den.why.t: Doʻkonda hurmat bilan **Dobrý deň** deb salomlashing. Ahoj! faqat doʻstlar, oila aʼzolari va bolalar uchun.

u1-l1.dobre-rano.note.en: For the early morning. Later in the day, switch to “Dobrý deň”.
u1-l1.dobre-rano.note.t: Erta tongda aytiladi. Kunning keyingi qismida «Dobrý deň» deysiz.

u1-l1.dovidenia.note.en: The polite goodbye: **Dovidenia, pani Horváthová** (Mrs Horváthová). With friends, “Ahoj!” works both ways.
u1-l1.dovidenia.note.t: Hurmat bilan xayrlashish: **Dovidenia, pani Horváthová** (Horvatova xonim). Doʻstlar bilan esa «Ahoj!» ham salom, ham xayr oʻrnida aytiladi.

u1-l1.dobru-noc.note.en: Only when someone goes to bed or you leave late at night. It is never a greeting.
u1-l1.dobru-noc.note.t: Faqat kimdir uxlashga ketayotganda yoki kechasi kech xayrlashganda aytiladi. Salomlashish uchun hech qachon ishlatilmaydi.

u1-l1.dobru-chut.note.en: Said to people who are about to eat. Notice the endings: dobr**ý** deň, dobr**é** ráno, dobr**ú** noc.
u1-l1.dobru-chut.note.t: Ovqatlanish oldidan aytiladi. Qoʻshimchalarga eʼtibor bering: dobr**ý** deň, dobr**é** ráno, dobr**ú** noc. «Yaxshi» soʻzining oxiri keyingi soʻzga qarab oʻzgaradi.

u1-l1.choice-dobru-noc.question.en: It's late and Lucia is going to bed. What do you say?
u1-l1.choice-dobru-noc.question.t: Kech boʻldi, Lusiya uxlashga ketyapti. Siz nima deysiz?

u1-l1.choice-dobru-noc.why.en: **Dobrú noc** is for when someone goes to bed. Dobrý večer and Dobré ráno are greetings, said when you meet.
u1-l1.choice-dobru-noc.why.t: **Dobrú noc** kimdir uxlashga ketayotganda aytiladi. Dobrý večer va Dobré ráno esa uchrashganda aytiladigan salomlar.

u1-l1.fill-dobre-rano-emma.why.en: Each greeting has its own ending: dobrý deň, **dobré** ráno, dobrú noc.
u1-l1.fill-dobre-rano-emma.why.t: Har bir salomning oʻz qoʻshimchasi bor: dobrý deň, **dobré** ráno, dobrú noc. Ularni shu holicha yodlang.

u1-l1.fill-dobru-chut-tomas.why.en: The ending -ú fits **chuť**, as in dobrú noc. Deň and večer take dobrý: dobrý deň, dobrý večer.
u1-l1.fill-dobru-chut-tomas.why.t: -ú qoʻshimchasi **chuť** soʻziga mos keladi, xuddi dobrú noc kabi. Deň va večer bilan esa dobrý keladi: dobrý deň, dobrý večer.

en: Pani Horváthová gets the polite goodbye, **Dovidenia**. Ahoj! is only for friends, family and children.
**Pani** is Mrs, for a woman: pani Horváthová. Pán is Mr, for a man, as in pán Kováč.
t: Horvatova xonimga hurmatli xayrlashuv kerak: **Dovidenia**. Ahoj! faqat doʻstlar, oila aʼzolari va bolalar uchun.
**Pani** — «xonim», ayolga aytiladi: pani Horváthová. Pán esa «janob», erkakka aytiladi: pán Kováč.

en: Večer takes **dobrý**, just like dobrý deň. The ending -ú goes with noc and chuť: dobrú noc.
**Pán** is Mr, for a man: pán Kováč. Pani is Mrs, for a woman, as in pani Horváthová.
Good evening is Dobrý **večer**, a greeting when you meet. Dobrú noc is only for bedtime, never a greeting.
t: Večer bilan **dobrý** keladi, xuddi dobrý deň kabi. -ú qoʻshimchasi esa noc va chuť bilan keladi: dobrú noc.
**Pán** — «janob», erkakka aytiladi: pán Kováč. Pani esa «xonim», ayolga aytiladi: pani Horváthová.
«Xayrli kech» — Dobrý **večer**, uchrashganda aytiladigan salom. Dobrú noc faqat uxlashdan oldin aytiladi, u salom emas.

u1-l2.dakujem.note.en: Warmer: **Ďakujem pekne.** = Thank you very much.

u1-l2.prosim.note.en: One word, many jobs. As a question, **Prosím?** means “Pardon?”
u1-l2.prosim.note.t: Bitta soʻz, koʻp vazifa. Savol ohangida **Prosím?** «Labbay? Nima dedingiz?» degani.

u1-l2.choice-prosim.question.en: Lucia says “Ďakujem.” What's the natural reply?
u1-l2.choice-prosim.question.t: Lusiya «Ďakujem» dedi. Eng tabiiy javob qaysi?

u1-l2.choice-prosim.why.en: The usual reply to ďakujem is **Prosím**: here it means you're welcome.
u1-l2.choice-prosim.why.t: Ďakujem (rahmat) deyishsa, odatda **Prosím** deb javob beriladi: bu yerda u «arzimaydi» degani.

u1-l2.nech-sa-paci.note.en: Say it when you hand something over, offer a seat or let someone go first.
u1-l2.nech-sa-paci.note.t: Biror narsani uzatganda, oʻrindiq taklif qilganda yoki kimnidir oldinga oʻtkazib yuborganda aytiladi.

u1-l2.choice-nech-sa-paci.question.en: Marek puts a plate of food in front of you. What does he say?
u1-l2.choice-nech-sa-paci.question.t: Marek oldingizga ovqat qoʻydi. U nima deydi?

u1-l2.ano-prosim.note.en: **Áno** = yes. The opposite: **Nie, ďakujem.** = No, thank you.

u1-l2.choice-nie-dakujem.question.en: Tomáš offers you a coffee, but you don't want one. What do you say?
u1-l2.choice-nie-dakujem.question.t: Tomash sizga qahva taklif qildi, lekin siz xohlamaysiz. Nima deysiz?

u1-l2.choice-nie-dakujem.why.en: Saying no to an offer is **Nie, ďakujem** (no, thank you). Áno, prosím (yes, please) would accept the coffee.
u1-l2.choice-nie-dakujem.why.t: Taklifni rad etish — **Nie, ďakujem** (yoʻq, rahmat). Áno, prosím (ha, iltimos) desangiz, qahvaga rozi boʻlgan boʻlasiz.

en: Thank you is **Ďakujem**. Prosím means please, or you're welcome as the reply to ďakujem.
**Pekne** makes the thanks warmer: thank you very much. Nie, ďakujem means no, thank you, turning an offer down.
t: «Rahmat» — **Ďakujem**. Prosím esa «iltimos», ďakujem soʻziga javoban esa «arzimaydi» degani.
**Pekne** minnatdorchilikni samimiyroq qiladi: «katta rahmat». Nie, ďakujem esa «yoʻq, rahmat», yaʼni taklifni rad etish.

u1-l2.prepacte.note.en: The polite form. To a friend, say **Prepáč!**
u1-l2.prepacte.note.t: Bu hurmat shakli. Doʻstga esa **Prepáč!** deysiz (xuddi «kechirasiz» oʻrniga «kechir» deganday).

u1-l2.nic-sa-nestalo.note.t: Kimdir «Prepáčte!» yoki «Prepáč!» desa, odatda shunday javob beriladi.

u1-l2.choice-prepacte.question.en: Emma bumps into pán Kováč in the corridor. What does she say?
u1-l2.choice-prepacte.question.t: Emma yoʻlakda janob Kovachga urilib ketdi. U nima deydi?

u1-l2.choice-prepacte.why.en: Bumping into someone calls for sorry, and pán Kováč gets the polite form: **Prepáčte!** To a friend, you'd say Prepáč!
u1-l2.choice-prepacte.why.t: Birovga urilib ketsangiz, kechirim soʻraysiz, janob Kovachga esa hurmat shakli kerak: **Prepáčte!** (kechirasiz). Doʻstga Prepáč! (kechir) deysiz.

u1-l2.fill-prepacte-nic-sa.why.en: The set reply is **Nič** sa nestalo, literally “nothing happened”. Nie just means no.
u1-l2.fill-prepacte-nic-sa.why.t: Tayyor javob — **Nič** sa nestalo, soʻzma-soʻz «hech narsa boʻlmadi». Nie esa shunchaki «yoʻq» degani.

u1-l2.na-zdravie.note.en: Say it when you raise a glass, and when someone sneezes.
u1-l2.na-zdravie.note.t: Qadah koʻtarganda va kimdir aksirganda aytiladi.

u1-l2.choice-na-zdravie.question.en: Tomáš sneezes. What do you say?

u1-l3.titleEn.en: How are you? What's your name?

u1-l3.ako-sa-mas.note.en: The friendly form, for friends and family. Literally “How do you have yourself?”
u1-l3.ako-sa-mas.note.t: Samimiy shakl: «sen» deb gaplashadigan doʻstlar va oila aʼzolari uchun.

u1-l3.mam-sa-dobre.note.en: **Mám sa dobre.** = I'm fine. **A ty?** = And you?

u1-l3.fill-ahoj-ako-sa.why.en: You're asking Tomáš about himself, so it's **máš** (you). Mám is for “I”: Mám sa dobre = I'm fine.
u1-l3.fill-ahoj-ako-sa.why.t: Siz Tomashning oʻzi haqida soʻrayapsiz, shuning uchun «sen» shakli kerak: **máš** (qalaysan). Mám esa «men» uchun: Mám sa dobre = Yaxshiman.

u1-l3.volam-sa-emma.note.en: Put in your own name: Volám sa…

en: You're giving your own name, so it's **Volám** sa (I). Voláš is for “you”: Ako sa voláš?
Your name goes with **Volám** sa, literally “I call myself”. Mám sa is about how you are: Mám sa dobre.
t: Oʻz ismingizni aytyapsiz, shuning uchun **Volám** sa («men»). Voláš esa «sen» uchun: Ako sa voláš?
Ism **Volám** sa bilan aytiladi, soʻzma-soʻz «oʻzimni chaqiraman». Mám sa esa hol-ahvol haqida: Mám sa dobre.

u1-l3.tesi-ma.note.en: The answer is **Aj mňa.** = Nice to meet you, too.

u1-l3.choice-aj-mna.question.en: Tomáš says “Teší ma.” What do you answer?
u1-l3.choice-aj-mna.question.t: Tomash «Teší ma» dedi. Siz nima deb javob berasiz?

u1-l3.choice-aj-mna.why.en: Teší ma is literally “it pleases me”, so the reply is **Aj mňa**, “me too”.
u1-l3.choice-aj-mna.why.t: Teší ma soʻzma-soʻz «meni xursand qiladi», shuning uchun javob **Aj mňa** — «meni ham».

u1-l3.fill-ahoj-ako-sa-2.en.en: Hi! What's your name? — My name is Lucia.

u1-l3.fill-ahoj-ako-sa-2.why.en: The reply gives a name, so the question needs **voláš** (What's your name?). Ako sa máš? asks how someone is.
u1-l3.fill-ahoj-ako-sa-2.why.t: Javobda ism aytilgan, demak savolda **voláš** boʻladi: «isming nima?». Ako sa máš? esa «qalaysan?» degani.

en: You're asking about the other person, so it's **máš** (you). Mám is for “I”: Mám sa dobre.
How are you? is Ako sa **máš**? Ako sa voláš? asks for someone's name.
t: Siz boshqa odamning ahvolini soʻrayapsiz, shuning uchun **máš** («sen»). Mám esa «men» uchun: Mám sa dobre.
«Qalaysan?» — Ako sa **máš**? Ako sa voláš? esa ismni soʻraydi.

u1-l4.titleEn.en: Ty or vy? Informal and polite

en: Slovak has two words for “you”. Say **ty** to friends, family and children. Say **vy** to strangers, older people and teachers, and to a group of people.
The verb shows which one you mean: in questions like these, the ty form ends in **-š** and the vy form in **-te**.
t: Slovak tilida ham, oʻzbek tilidagidek, ikki xil murojaat bor: **ty** = sen, **vy** = siz. **ty** doʻstlar, oila aʼzolari va bolalarga aytiladi. **vy** notanish odamlarga, yoshi kattalarga, oʻqituvchilarga, shuningdek bir guruh odamlarga aytiladi.
Feʼlning oxiri ham buni koʻrsatadi: bunday savollarda ty shakli **-š** bilan, vy shakli **-te** bilan tugaydi. Oʻzbek tilida ham shunday: qalaysan — qalaysiz.

en: Hello, Mr Kováč. How are you?
Do you speak Slovak? — Yes, a little.

u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate.question.en: Emma meets pani Horváthová, her teacher. Which question fits?
u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate.question.t: Emma oʻqituvchisi Horvatova xonimni uchratdi. Qaysi savol mos keladi?

u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate.why.en: A teacher gets **vy**, so the verb ends in **-te**: má**te**. Máš is the ty form, for friends and family.
u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate.why.t: Oʻqituvchiga **vy** (siz) deyiladi, shuning uchun feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi: má**te**. Máš — ty (sen) shakli, doʻstlar va oila uchun.

u1-l4.fill-ahoj-tomas-ako.why.en: Ahoj and a friend's name mean **ty**, so the verb ends in **-š**: má**š**. Máte is for vy.
u1-l4.fill-ahoj-tomas-ako.why.t: Ahoj va doʻstning ismi — demak **ty** (sen), shuning uchun feʼl **-š** bilan tugaydi: má**š**. Máte esa vy (siz) uchun.

u1-l4.fill-dobry-den-ako.why.en: **Dobrý deň** is the polite hello, so ask with vy: the verb ends in **-te**, volá**te**.
u1-l4.fill-dobry-den-ako.why.t: **Dobrý deň** — hurmatli salom, shuning uchun vy (siz) bilan soʻrang: feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi, volá**te**.

en: A polite question takes **vy**, so the verb ends in **-te**: Hovorí**te**. Hovoríš is the ty form, for friends and family.
t: Hurmat bilan soʻralganda **vy** (siz) ishlatiladi, shuning uchun feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi: Hovorí**te**. Hovoríš — ty (sen) shakli, doʻstlar va oila uchun.

u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate-2.question.en: Emma meets Lucia and Tomáš together. How does she ask how they are?
u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate-2.question.t: Emma Lusiya va Tomashni birga uchratdi. Ularning ahvolini qanday soʻraydi?

u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate-2.why.en: **Vy** is also for a group, even of friends, so the verb ends in **-te**: má**te**. Máš is for one friend.
u1-l4.choice-ako-sa-mate-2.why.t: **Vy** guruhga ham aytiladi, hatto ular doʻstlar boʻlsa ham, shuning uchun feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi: má**te**. Máš — bitta doʻst uchun.

u1-l4.grammar-same-phrase-ty.title.t: Bitta ibora: ty va vy shakli

en: Many everyday phrases have a ty form and a vy form. The vy form often just adds **-te**.
With vy, say hello with **Dobrý deň** and goodbye with **Dovidenia**. Meeting a group of friends? Say **Ahojte!**
t: Koʻp kundalik iboralarning ty shakli ham, vy shakli ham bor. Koʻpincha vy shaklida oxiriga shunchaki **-te** qoʻshiladi.
vy bilan gaplashganda **Dobrý deň** deb salomlashing va **Dovidenia** deb xayrlashing. Bir guruh doʻstlaringizni uchratdingizmi? **Ahojte!** deng.

en: Enjoy your meal! — Thank you, you too.

u1-l4.choice-aj-tebe.question.en: Lucia says “Dobrú noc!” What does Emma answer?
u1-l4.choice-aj-tebe.question.t: Lusiya «Dobrú noc!» dedi. Emma nima deb javob beradi?

u1-l4.choice-aj-tebe.why.en: Lucia is Emma's friend, so Emma uses ty: Aj **tebe**. Aj vám is for vy.
u1-l4.choice-aj-tebe.why.t: Lusiya — Emmaning doʻsti, shuning uchun Emma ty (sen) ishlatadi: Aj **tebe** (senga ham). Aj vám (sizga ham) — vy uchun.

u1-l4.fill-dobru-chut-emma.en.en: Enjoy your meal, Emma! — Thank you, you too, Mrs Horváthová.
u1-l4.fill-dobru-chut-emma.en.t: Yoqimli ishtaha, Emma! — Rahmat, sizga ham, Horvatova xonim.

u1-l4.fill-dobru-chut-emma.why.en: Pani Horváthová is Emma's teacher, so Emma uses vy: aj **vám**. Aj tebe is for friends.
u1-l4.fill-dobru-chut-emma.why.t: Horvatova xonim — Emmaning oʻqituvchisi, shuning uchun Emma vy (siz) ishlatadi: aj **vám** (sizga ham). Aj tebe — doʻstlar uchun.

en: Lucia is one friend, so use ty: **Maj** sa! Majte sa, with -te, is for vy or a group.
Take care is **Maj** sa. Ahojte! is hello to a group of friends, and Lucia is just one person.
t: Lusiya — bitta doʻst, shuning uchun ty (sen): **Maj** sa! -te bilan Majte sa esa vy (siz) yoki guruh uchun.
«Yaxshi qol» — **Maj** sa. Ahojte! esa bir guruh doʻstlarga aytiladigan salom, Lusiya esa bitta odam.

u1-l4.fill-ahoj-emma-vitaj.why.en: Ahoj and one friend, Emma, mean ty: **Vitaj**. Vitajte, with -te, is for vy or a group.
u1-l4.fill-ahoj-emma-vitaj.why.t: Ahoj va bitta doʻst, Emma — demak ty (sen): **Vitaj** (xush kelibsan). -te bilan Vitajte esa vy (siz) yoki guruh uchun.

en: The little hook is called **mäkčeň**. On c, s, z it gives the sounds in “**ch**ip”, “**sh**ip” and “plea**s**ure”: č, š, ž.

On d, t, n, l it makes the sound soft, as if a short “y” followed: ď, ť, ň, ľ. Before **e** and **i** these usually sound soft even without the hook: **de**ň, **Te**ší ma. Before **y** they stay hard: **ty**.
**ch** is a single letter. It sounds like “ch” in Scottish “lo**ch**”.
t: Harf ustidagi kichik qalpoqcha **mäkčeň** deb ataladi. c, s, z ustida u oʻzbekcha ch, sh va j («jurnal»dagi kabi) tovushlarini beradi: č, š, ž. Qalpoqchasiz **c** esa ts kabi oʻqiladi: noc (tun).

d, t, n, l ustida u tovushni yumshatadi, goʻyo ortidan qisqa «y» kelgandek: ď, ť, ň, ľ. **e** va **i** oldidan bu harflar qalpoqchasiz ham odatda yumshoq oʻqiladi: **de**ň, **Te**ší ma. **y** oldidan esa qattiq qoladi: **ty**.
**ch** — bitta harf. U oʻzbekcha x kabi oʻqiladi: Dobrú **ch**uť. Oʻzbekcha ch tovushi esa **č** bilan yoziladi.

en: The mark on á, é, í, ó, ú, ý is called **dĺžeň**. It makes the vowel long: hold it about twice as long. **y** and **ý** sound just like **i** and **í**.
Stress is easy: it is always on the **first** syllable, even when a later vowel is long: **Do**brý deň, **Ďa**kujem, **Do**videnia.
t: á, é, í, ó, ú, ý ustidagi chiziqcha **dĺžeň** deb ataladi. U unlini choʻziq qiladi: uni taxminan ikki baravar uzunroq ayting. **y** va **ý** xuddi **i** va **í** kabi oʻqiladi.

Urgʻu oson: u doim **birinchi** boʻgʻinga tushadi, keyingi unli choʻziq boʻlsa ham: **Do**brý deň, **Ďa**kujem, **Do**videnia. Oʻzbek tilida urgʻu odatda oxirgi boʻgʻinga tushadi, shuning uchun bunga eʼtibor bering.

u1-l5.choice-tesi-ma.why.en: **š** is the “sh” in “ship”: Te**š**í ma. The č in Čau! is the “ch” in “chip”.
u1-l5.choice-tesi-ma.why.t: **š** oʻzbekcha «sh» kabi oʻqiladi: Te**š**í ma. Čau! soʻzidagi č esa oʻzbekcha «ch».

u1-l5.choice-dovidenia.why.en: Stress is always on the first syllable, even in a long word: **Do**videnia.
u1-l5.choice-dovidenia.why.t: Urgʻu doim **birinchi** boʻgʻinga tushadi, uzun soʻzda ham: **Do**videnia. Oʻzbekchadagidek oxirgi boʻgʻinga emas.

u1-l5.fill-mam-sa-dobre.why.en: With a short e, **dobre** means fine or well: Mám sa dobre. Dobré, with a long é, goes with ráno.
u1-l5.fill-mam-sa-dobre.why.t: Qisqa e bilan **dobre** «yaxshi» degani: Mám sa dobre. Choʻziq é bilan dobré esa ráno bilan keladi.

u1-l5.fill-dobre-rano.why.en: Good morning has a long é: **Dobré** ráno. Dobre, with a short e, means fine: Mám sa dobre.
u1-l5.fill-dobre-rano.why.t: «Xayrli tong»da choʻziq é bor: **Dobré** ráno. Qisqa e bilan dobre esa «yaxshi» degani: Mám sa dobre.

u1-l5.choice-den.question.en: Which word has a soft ň?

u1-l5.choice-den.why.en: The hook (mäkčeň) on n makes it soft, like “ny” in “canyon”: de**ň**. Noc and ráno have a plain n.
u1-l5.choice-den.why.t: n ustidagi qalpoqcha (mäkčeň) uni yumshoq qiladi, goʻyo ortidan qisqa «y» kelgandek: de**ň**. Noc va ráno soʻzlarida n oddiy.

u1-l5.grammar-o-ia-ie.title.en: ä, ô and ia, ie, iu
u1-l5.grammar-o-ia-ie.title.t: ä, ô va ia, ie, iu

en: **ä** usually sounds like the “e” in “bed”: p**ä**ť (five). **ô** sounds like “wo”: st**ô**l (table) sounds like “stwol”.
**ia**, **ie** and **iu** glide together into one syllable: Dovide**nia**, Na zdrav**ie**, N**ie**.
t: **ä** odatda oʻzbekcha «e» kabi oʻqiladi: p**ä**ť (besh). **ô** «uo» kabi oʻqiladi: st**ô**l (stol) taxminan «stuol» boʻlib eshitiladi.
**ia**, **ie** va **iu** bitta boʻgʻinga qoʻshilib ketadi (taxminan «ya», «ye», «yu» kabi): Dovide**nia**, Na zdrav**ie**, N**ie**.

u1-l5.choice-nie.why.en: **ie** glides together into one syllable, so N**ie** has just one, like Na zdrav**ie**.
u1-l5.choice-nie.why.t: **ie** bitta boʻgʻinga qoʻshilib ketadi (taxminan «ye»), shuning uchun N**ie** — bitta boʻgʻin, xuddi Na zdrav**ie** iborasidagi kabi.

u1-l5.choice-stol.question.en: Which word has ô, the “wo” sound?
u1-l5.choice-stol.question.t: Qaysi soʻzda ô, yaʼni «uo» tovushi bor?

u1-l5.choice-stol.why.en: **ô** sounds like “wo”: st**ô**l sounds like “stwol”. Päť has ä, like the e in “bed”.
u1-l5.choice-stol.why.t: **ô** «uo» kabi oʻqiladi: st**ô**l taxminan «stuol» boʻlib eshitiladi. Päť soʻzida esa ä bor, u oʻzbekcha «e» kabi.

en: With a short e, **dobre** means fine or well: Mám sa dobre. Dobré, with a long é, goes with ráno: Dobré ráno.
You're saying how you are yourself, so it's **Mám** (I). Máš is for “you”: Ako sa máš?
t: Qisqa e bilan **dobre** «yaxshi» degani: Mám sa dobre. Choʻziq é bilan dobré esa ráno bilan keladi: Dobré ráno.
Siz oʻz ahvolingizni aytyapsiz, shuning uchun **Mám** («men»). Máš esa «sen» uchun: Ako sa máš?

u1-pisanie.listen-tesi-ma-aj.en.en: Nice to meet you. — Nice to meet you, too.

u1-l6.choice-dobre-rano.question.en: You meet pani Horváthová early in the morning. What do you say?
u1-l6.choice-dobre-rano.question.t: Erta tongda Horvatova xonimni uchratdingiz. Nima deysiz?

u1-l6.choice-dobre-rano.why.en: Early in the morning, say **Dobré ráno**, polite enough for a teacher. Ahoj! is only for friends, and Dobrú noc is for bedtime.
u1-l6.choice-dobre-rano.why.t: Erta tongda **Dobré ráno** deng: bu oʻqituvchiga ham yetarlicha hurmatli. Ahoj! faqat doʻstlar uchun, Dobrú noc esa uxlashdan oldin aytiladi.

en: Ahoj and one friend, Lucia, mean **ty**, so the verb ends in **-š**: má**š**. Máte is for vy.
How are you? is Ako sa **máš**? Ako sa voláš? asks for someone's name.
t: Ahoj va bitta doʻst, Lusiya — demak **ty** (sen), shuning uchun feʼl **-š** bilan tugaydi: má**š**. Máte esa vy (siz) uchun.
«Qalaysan?» — Ako sa **máš**? Ako sa voláš? esa ismni soʻraydi.

u1-l6.fill-dobru-noc-emma.en.en: Good night, Emma! — You too, Lucia.
u1-l6.fill-dobru-noc-emma.en.t: Xayrli tun, Emma! — Senga ham, Lusiya.

u1-l6.fill-dobru-noc-emma.why.en: Lucia is a friend, so use ty: Aj **tebe**. Aj vám is for vy: teachers, strangers or a group.
u1-l6.fill-dobru-noc-emma.why.t: Lusiya — doʻst, shuning uchun ty (sen): Aj **tebe**. Aj vám esa vy (siz) uchun: oʻqituvchilar, notanishlar yoki guruh.

en: When you didn't catch what someone said

u1-l6.choice-prosim.why.en: Said as a question, **Prosím?** means Pardon? On its own, prosím is please or you're welcome.
u1-l6.choice-prosim.why.t: Savol ohangida **Prosím?** «Nima dedingiz?» degani. Oddiy holda prosím — «iltimos» yoki «arzimaydi».

u1-l6.fill-dobry-den-pan.en.en: Hello, Mr Kováč. How are you?

u1-l6.fill-dobry-den-pan.why.en: Pán Kováč gets vy (note the polite Dobrý deň), so the verb ends in **-te**: má**te**.
u1-l6.fill-dobry-den-pan.why.t: Janob Kovachga vy (siz) deyiladi (hurmatli salom Dobrý deň ham shuni koʻrsatadi), shuning uchun feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi: má**te**.

en: The set reply is **Nič** sa nestalo, literally “nothing happened”. Nie just means no.
That's OK is Nič sa **nestalo**, literally “nothing happened”. Páči belongs in Nech sa páči, here you go.
t: Tayyor javob — **Nič** sa nestalo, soʻzma-soʻz «hech narsa boʻlmadi». Nie esa shunchaki «yoʻq» degani.
«Hech qisi yoʻq» — Nič sa **nestalo**, soʻzma-soʻz «hech narsa boʻlmadi». Páči esa Nech sa páči («marhamat») iborasidan.

u1-l6.choice-ahojte.why.en: For a group of friends, add **-te**: Ahoj**te**! Ahoj! is for one friend, and Maj sa! means take care.
u1-l6.choice-ahojte.why.t: Bir guruh doʻstlarga **-te** qoʻshing: Ahoj**te**! Ahoj! — bitta doʻstga, Maj sa! esa «yaxshi qol» degani.

u1-l6.build-volam-sa-emma.prompt.en: My name is Emma. Nice to meet you.

en: You're giving your own name, so it's **Volám** sa (I). Voláš is for “you”: Ako sa voláš?
Nice to meet you is Teší **ma**. Mňa belongs in the reply: Aj mňa, nice to meet you too.
t: Oʻz ismingizni aytyapsiz, shuning uchun **Volám** sa («men»). Voláš esa «sen» uchun: Ako sa voláš?
«Tanishganimdan xursandman» — Teší **ma**. Mňa esa javobda keladi: Aj mňa, «men ham xursandman».

u1-l6.fill-hovorite-po-slovensky.en.en: Do you speak Slovak? — Yes, a little.
